To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RF-based emotion recognition from wireless network edge is feasible and can be applied in real environments with high accuracy.

RFexpress! can detect emotion from movement, gestures and poses at the network edge in realistic and noisy environments with high accuracy and that it is able to do this with a very low number of sensors (1-3) in contrast to other approaches that need 10s or 100s of cameras.

(1) RFexpress! is the first system to recognize emotion at the wireless network-edge; (2) it is able to recognize emotion from RF-fluctuations in vehicular and indoor environments; (3) RFexpress! achieves recognition accuracy of up to 82.9%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploiting the wireless network edge to sense emotion and activities from RF-fluctuations.
a new paradigm of emotion sensing via RF-fluctuation.
the question of how to exploit wireless network edge for DFAR emotion and behaviour recognition in realistic environments and under realistic conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the edge-based system can be used to reliably recognize emotion and activity in a vehicular and a static setting in real environments.
RFexpress! is the first-ever system for emotion sensing at the network edge, which is robust against variations in SNR and is able to achieve high accuracy in realistic environments.
RFexpress! is a reliable and effective edge-based system to recognise emotion from movement, pose and gesture via DFAR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can achieve high recognition accuracy with a system that is not only low-power and low-cost, but also highly scalable and robust to environmental changes.
RFexpress! is able to achieve high accuracies for activity recognition at the wireless network’s edge, in a wide range of environments and under different SNR conditions.
we can reliably exploit the wireless network edge to detect risky driving behavior and agitated human behavior from RF fluctuations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wireless network edge is a rich source of information for environmental perception.
the edge-based RF-based emotion recognition can be deployed in realistic environments with reasonable accuracies.
the wireless network edge can be exploited as a sensing platform for emotion and activity recognition in realistic settings.
